identity.name: TEXMACO RAIL & ENG. LTD.
identity.industry: Rail Freight Rolling Stock, Foundry & Rail Electrification

summary.oneLiner: Texmaco reported a transient revenue dip in Q3FY26 due to persistent wheel-set shortages and export headwinds, but management signaled an inflection point with resuming exports and a strategic pivot toward higher-margin segments (propulsion, metro, foundry) under 'Texmaco 2.0' to double revenue in 3-5 years.

one-line thesis: Texmaco reported a transient revenue dip in Q3FY26 due to persistent wheel-set shortages and export headwinds, but management signaled an inflection point with resuming exports and a strategic pivot toward higher-margin segments (propulsion, metro, foundry) under 'Texmaco 2.0' to double revenue in 3-5 years.
financial scorecard: Revenue: Rs.1,042cr (Q3), Rs.3,210cr (9M) - moderated YoY due to 20-25% lower wagon volumes; EBITDA: Rs.102cr (Q3), Rs.313cr (9M) ~9.7% margin - pressured by operating leverage not structural issues; PAT: Rs.42cr (Q3), Rs.136cr (9M); Order Book: Rs.5,661cr (as of Dec 2025); Net Debt: ~Rs.800cr; One-offs: US tariff impact reduced foundry exports by 30% YoY; Wheel-set availability constrained production to 60-65% of potential.
guidance: Revenue: Targeting 2x growth in 3-5 years ('Texmaco 2.0'); Margin: Focus on richer product mix to improve EBITDA beyond current ~9.7%; Order Inflow: Expecting large railway tenders soon; Capex: Rs.75-80cr projected for FY26.
order book & pipeline: Total Rs.5,661cr: Wagons Rs.2,140cr (~4,900 units: 3,000 IR, 1,400 Private, 600 Export); Rail Electrification Rs.1,800cr; Rail Infra Rs.511cr; Others Rs.1,000cr. Wagon book covers ~2 quarters of production.
segment / subsidiary detail: Wagons: 2,027 units delivered in Q3 (6,176 in 9M); Foundry: 7,646 MT in Q3 (25,326 MT in 9M) - exports resuming after tariff hit; Electrification/Infra: Turning around with government capex tailwinds; New Initiatives: Propulsion, Metro/EMU coaches, Iron Pellets.
growth verticals / optionality: Entry into propulsion systems, Kavach safety tech, Metro/EMU coach manufacturing, Global Capability Center (design services), Iron Pellet mining vertical, and expanded private wagon leasing.
margins & cost dynamics: EBITDA margin ~9.7% impacted by fixed cost absorption on lower volumes; Management focusing on purchase cost negotiation and fixed cost moderation to protect margins despite volume volatility.
capex / expansion: 9M FY26 spend: Rs.40cr + Rs.40cr committed; FY26 full year guidance: Rs.75-80cr. Future capex for new verticals (propulsion/metro) to be 'sensible' and potentially via JVs to avoid disproportionate outlay.
capital allocation: Debt reduction prioritized as operating cash flow improves (historically low due to working capital build-up and acquisitions); Strategic M&A (e.g., Jindal tech) yielding returns (Rs.230cr PBT in 21 months); Divestment/Leasing restructuring to attract private players.
risks & watch-items: Continued wheel-set supply bottlenecks from government; Delay in large Indian Railway tender announcements; Global geopolitical/tariff volatility affecting foundry exports; Execution risk in new verticals (Metro/Propulsion).
management quality / tone: Cautiously optimistic; Acknowledges short-term pain (wheel-sets, exports) but emphasizes structural strength, diversification ('Texmaco 2.0'), and imminent recovery in H2/FY27.
non-obvious takeaways: Acquisition of Jindal's wagon tech (Rs.650cr) is already profitable (Rs.230cr PBT in 21 months) and enables niche private/export wagons; Multimodal wagons (FMP/CMP) prototypes validated with unique market position; Foundry export schedule already doubled (7,500 MT) with path to 20,000 MT.
challenges → beneficiaries & losers:
| Challenge | Beneficiary/Loser | Dir | Conviction | Note |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Wheel-set shortage limiting production volume | Titan Freight Solutions | beneficiary | Med | If Texmaco cannot fulfill private orders due to IR wheel constraints, private lessors may source from competitors or lease existing stock, though Texmaco is also expanding leasing. |
| US/EU tariff pressures on foundry exports | BEML Ltd | beneficiary | Low | Competitor in rail space; if Texmaco's export recovery lags, BEML could capture share, though Texmaco claims exports have resumed. |
| Need for diversified rolling stock suppliers | RVNL | beneficiary | High | Texmaco's pending JV with RVNL (shareholder agreement finalizing) positions RVNL to benefit from Texmaco's manufacturing scale and new tech capabilities. |

themes.title: Railway rolling-stock & component capex
themes.need: A ~INR2.65 lakh cr Railways capital outlay and a pending ~1-lakh-wagon tender ('anytime this year' per JWL) drive rolling-stock, wheelsets, springs, castings, bogie components and interiors - with deep import-substitution (Neetu Yoshi 544434 castings; Airfloa 544516 interiors; Concord 543619 electronics). TITAGARH/TEXRAIL/JWL lead wagons; RVNL/IRCON/GPTINFRA on rail EPC.
themes.driver: Indian Railways large wagon tender award (next 1-2 quarters); wheelset plant ramp; Vande Bharat / Kavach orders.

business_model.title: Positioning (investor deck)
business_model.body:
- "One of the largest suppliers of Freight Cars in India, manufacturing one out of every four Wagons on the IR network", with a manufacturing record of 50,000+ freight cars supplied over the last 20 years including 7,000+ supplied to private customers over the last 10 years.
- "Leading position in the export of Freight Cars and railway components for 50 years", with an export track record of 550+ freight cars over 3 years and a claim to be "one of the leading exporter of railway castings from India, supplying to global markets and benefiting from geopolitical shifts in supply chains".
- Management frames the moat as integration: "Texmaco benefits from its integrated capabilities across wagon manufacturing, rail infrastructure, foundry products and engineering solutions", combined with a geographically diversified order book.
- "One of the largest foundry to be accredited by the Association of American Railroad (AAR)" and "a leading company working with mild-steel, stainless steel and composite materials for manufacturing of rolling stock solutions".
- Consolidated order book of Rs 9,923 Cr as on June 30, 2026, after securing orders worth over Rs 5,200 crore during the quarter across Freight Rolling Stock, Railway Signalling, Electrification and Transmission Infrastructure.

other.title: Notable from the deck
other.body:
- [Leasing platform] The Company "strengthened its strategic partnership with Trinity Rail Global Inc. through its participation in the Touax Texmaco Railcar Leasing platform", combining Trinity Rail's global leasing expertise, Touax's established platform and Texmaco's manufacturing and engineering capabilities to create "India's first globally benchmarked railcar leasing platform".
- [JV structure] Four named partnerships: Touax Texmaco (50%) leasing freight cars long term to private sector logistics and industrial transportation companies in India; Nymwag Texmaco (51%) for wagons and components; Wabtec Texmaco (40%) for braking systems and components for the Indian and US markets; and Saira Asia (51%) for passenger coach railway interiors in Vadodara.
- [Policy tailwind] 8 new railway reforms announced by the Government and an Indian Railways plan for Rs 13 Lakhs crore freight-led expansion, with Vande Bharat, Kavach, Dedicated Freight Corridors and Station Redevelopment cited as continuing to expand opportunities across the rail value chain.
- [Industry milestone] "India's first Vande Bharat Freight EMU successfully achieved 145 kmph during trials, supporting the development of high-speed freight logistics for time-sensitive cargo, e-commerce, parcels and cold-chain transportation."
- [Recognition] Won the Star Performer award in the Large Industrial Category at the National Export Excellence Award 2024-25, alongside an Excellence in Logistics Award (June 2026).
